scope_assumption: Passenger corridors used by LARy and Yellow Car successors, 1895–1963, including documented temporary physical alignments. Yards, freight-only spurs and predecessor-only tracks remain separate optional categories.
peak_year_note: 1924 is cited as a peak in Metro’s collection summary, but this is not a verified maximum of the union of physical corridors. Later additions and earlier removals are documented.
what_was_completed: Source discovery, download and schema inspection; separate WGS84 conversions; combined observations overlay; targeted chronology review. No complete segment-by-segment historical or geographic reconciliation.
merge_plan: Keep raw source layers immutable and individually selectable.
Audit early-only, intermediate temporary, late terminal and optional facility segments into separate correction layers.
Choose canonical geometry for each physical corridor; split at junctions and realignments. Keep source IDs and observation dates.
Reconcile positional differences manually before snapping; close parallel lines may represent real alternatives.
Combine accepted segments into a separate cumulative layer. Retain references to all contributing observations; dissolve only genuinely shared geometry.
Store observed_on separately from opened_on, closed_on and track_removed_on. Route transfers do not necessarily mean construction or abandonment.
Mark unresolved segments and unknown dates explicitly. Claim completeness only after every route-history change and selected facility scope is accounted for.
